note: Tightly packed struct-of-arrays: every field is one contiguous run of recordCount values at the stated byteOffset. Index i of each array refers to the same object; designations are in ngc-ids.json at the same index. Fields are ordered 4-byte, then 2-byte, then 1-byte, so every byteOffset is a multiple of its dtype size and each field can be wrapped in a zero-copy typed-array view over the ArrayBuffer.

fields.name: distancePc
fields.note: kind 1 = 1000/parallax_mas; kind 2 = Hubble distance z*c/H0 with H0 = 67.66 km/s/Mpc, c = 299792.458 km/s (Planck 2018)

fields.name: posAng
fields.units: degree, major-axis position angle north eastwards

fields.name: surfBr
fields.units: mag/arcsec^2 (B-band, within the 25 mag isophote; galaxies only)

fields.name: messier
fields.note: 0 = not a Messier object, else the Messier number 1..110

rule: Extragalactic types (G, GPair, GTrpl, GGroup) with a positive heliocentric redshift get a Hubble distance. Their OpenNGC parallax is ignored: it is SIMBADs "main value", which for a galaxy is a contaminated foreground measurement (it would place M31 at 167 pc).

Galactic types with a positive parallax get 1000/parallax_mas. Their redshift is ignored: it is a peculiar radial velocity, not cosmological expansion, and cz/H0 would place the Orion Nebula at 412 kpc instead of 412 pc.
Everything else is direction-only (distancePc = NaN, distanceKind = 0) and must be drawn on the celestial sphere, not in depth. No distance is estimated, interpolated or invented.
Notably M31/NGC0224 is direction-only here: it is blueshifted, so Hubbles law yields nothing, and its true 785 kpc rests on Cepheid/TRGB work that OpenNGC does not carry.

cosmology.formula: distancePc = z * c / H0 * 1e6  (valid only for z << 1)
cosmology.caveat: Below z ~ 0.01 (~44 Mpc) peculiar velocities of several hundred km/s are a large fraction of cz, so those 2577 Hubble distances are indicative only. Badge them DERIVED, never MEASURED.

companions.ngc-ids.json: index-aligned designations, constellations and Hubble morphological types
companions.ngc-names.json: objects carrying a common name and/or a Messier number
